subject: PrivDeploy identity: entitlement mapping, firewall, SCIM sync
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Brian Kelly <brian.kelly@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: PrivDeploy identity kickoff: quick checklist

Brian —

Thanks for taking the time to start the identity handoff for the private control plane deployment. To keep the cutover smooth, can you confirm the items below and attach any artifacts you already have? I attached our master checklist for reference.

Primary asks:
- SAML IdP metadata (entityID, ACS, signature algorithm) — do you host metadata at a URL or will you share the XML?
- SCIM: base URL and whether you support /scim/v2 and delta tokens. Any documented rate limits?
- Group attribute name in SAML assertions (e.g., "groups" vs "memberOf"). Do you include nested groups?
- Firewall: source IPs we should allow for webhook/SCIM inbound and what ports are open outbound from your VPC to our control-plane endpoints (usually 443).
- Long-lived service account for SCIM writes vs short-lived OAuth client — which do you prefer?

Proposed next steps: you share SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint + an initial allowlist, we validate against our dev control plane, then schedule a short sync window for a test delta run.

Attachments: priv-deploy-id-checklist.xlsx

Best,
Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Brian Kelly <brian.kelly@acmecloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-03T12:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy identity kickoff: quick checklist

On Mon, Nov 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com> wrote:
> Brian —
>
> Thanks for taking the time to start the identity handoff for the private control plane deployment.

Thanks Laura — quick answers below and attaching our SAML metadata.

SAML
- We host metadata at https://idp.acmecloud.com/metadata.xml (attached: acme-saml-metadata.xml).
- IdP: Okta (enterprise), signature algorithm RSA-SHA256, EntityID: https://idp.acmecloud.com
- Assertion will include attribute "groups" and we can provide both fully-expanded group DNs and a short name attribute.

SCIM
- Base URL: https://idp.acmecloud.com/scim/v2
- Supports /Users and /Groups, supports delta using startIndex/totalResults (we currently do nightly deltas).
- Rate limits: 600 requests/minute; we can provide a lower burst for partners if needed.
- We plan to use a client credential (service account) for SCIM writes; token rotation policy is 90 days.

Firewall / Networking
- Allowlist for inbound to our systems: 52.24.16.0/24 and 3.210.45.0/24 (we will also accept callbacks from dynamic ranges via TLS with mTLS optional).
- Outbound connections: we only require HTTPS (443) to your control plane endpoints.

We can do a test delta next Wednesday (2025-11-05) morning your time.

Regards,
Brian Kelly
Identity Engineering, AcmeCloud
brian.kelly@acmecloud.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Brian Kelly <brian.kelly@acmecloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T08:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy identity kickoff: quick checklist

Thanks for the details, Brian — this is helpful. A few clarifications and a proposed mapping so the ops team can prepare firewall changes and role binding templates.

1) SAML attribute mapping - Redwood expects a claim we call "role_claims" (array) in our control plane that we map to local entitlements (admin, operator, viewer). If you can supply the short group names we can map them explicitly. Proposed mapping:
  - acme:infra-admin -> redwood:admin
  - acme:infra-operator -> redwood:operator
  - acme:infra-view -> redwood:viewer

2) SCIM provisioning- happy to use a client credentials flow for SCIM writes. For auditability we will create dedicated SCIM user 'redwood-scim-client' with a restricted OAuth scope. Confirm that the 90-day rotation is compatible with your automation; we can support manual rotation windows if needed.

3) Network notes- we will need to open our control-plane inbound for your SCIM service to POST/PUT (443). For the test run, allowlisting the two /24s you provided is fine. If you plan to use additional AWS ranges later, we will prefer mTLS so allowlist expansion isn't required.

4) Rate limiting and retry semantics- we'll implement exponential backoff with a 429-aware retry loop; please confirm whether you return Retry-After headers on 429s (helps).

Action items from our side:
- Laura: confirm internal test control-plane instance and create temp route for scim staging.
- Soojin: validate mTLS certificate expectations and rotation policy for the control-plane certs.
- I will produce a role-binding template and a short-runbook for rotation and emergency rollback.

Can we lock the test delta for 2025-11-05T09:00-10:00 PT? If that works we'll open a calendar invite and a shared Drive folder (link in metadata).

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Platform Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-04T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy identity kickoff: quick checklist

Folks — short technical notes from infra/security regarding SCIM and SAML for privdeploy. Attaching our SCIM guidance doc (scim-rate-limits.pdf).

- SCIM deltas: we prefer RFC 7644 incremental sync (ETag/If-None-Match where supported). If your provider only does nightly full sync, we can handle it but the runbook changes (longer maintenance window).
- Rate limits: we'll honor 429 + Retry-After. For the test window please keep traffic below 200 req/min to the staging endpoint. Production can be negotiated once we validate behavior.
- Service account: create a non-human OAuth client with an aud claim scoped to scim:write and scim:read. Put the client secret into our vault via the shared Drive flow (we'll provide a signed upload URL).
- SAML assertion timing: please limit NotBefore/NotOnOrAfter skew to under 5 minutes, and include NameID in transient and persistent formats for different flows.
- mTLS: optional for now, recommended for production. If you can present a client cert during the test, we'll accept it but fallback to token auth is fine.

I'll prepare the runbook snippets for handling delta failures (rollback step, canonical recover path) and post to Drive after Marcus creates the folder.

Irene Choi
Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com

From: Acme Security <acme-security@acmecloud.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Brian Kelly <brian.kelly@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy identity kickoff: quick checklist

Marcus / Laura —

We confirm the test delta window for 2025-11-05 09:00-10:00 PT. Networking team will open the two /24 ranges you listed and expect to close them after verification; we will provide a temporary VPN jumpbox if needed. We attached the signed SAML metadata earlier; token rotation for the SCIM client is acceptable at 90 days and we will add automation hooks for emergency rotation.

Please send the calendar invite and Drive link. We'll have a security observer and one engineer on the call. If you require mTLS proof for production we can follow up with certificate exchange.

Thanks,
Acme Security Team
acme-security@acmecloud.com
